Alex —

Thanks for the detailed list. I’m the solutions engineer on this thread — below are concise answers and notes. Happy to walk through examples during the technical deep dive.

1) CMEK / At-rest encryption: 
- For Hosted Redwood API we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) via envelope encryption. The data (blobs/objects and model artifacts) are encrypted at-rest with AES-256; the data encryption keys (DEKs) are wrapped with a customer-provided key (KEK) in their KMS.
- This means you can provide a KMS key (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault) that we use to protect the DEKs. We do not hold the plaintext KEK.
- Note: for some managed components (e.g., shared model cache) we provide a per-tenant envelope; we can scope the KEK usage so only your tenant’s DEKs are wrapped with your key.

2) HSM support (BYOK / CloudHSM): 
- We support HSM-backed keys via AWS CloudHSM-backed KMS and HSM-backed key stores in GCP/Azure for Hosted customers. For Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments we support direct integration with customer HSMs (FIPS 140-2/3 compatible hardware: Thales, Luna, etc.).
- Integration notes: for hosted CMEK you provide a KMS key ARN or key resource; to use HSM-backed keys ensure your KMS key is configured as HSM-protected. For Private deployments we can run a local HSM or integrate with your on-prem HSM over mutual-TLS.

3) Key rotation & effects: 
- We recommend rotating KEKs in KMS at least annually; rotating the DEK wrapping key (KEK) does not require re-encrypting stored data if you use KMS re-wrap operations — KMS handles re-wrapping DEKs.
- If you rotate your root KEK and your KMS supports re-wrap, the stored DEKs stay valid after a re-wrap; for environments without re-wrap you’d schedule a re-encryption job (we can assist).
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: embeddings stored in our object store are encrypted at-rest the same as other objects. Rotation does not invalidate embeddings provided KEK/DEK are managed correctly.

4) Auditability / logs: 
- KMS usage logs (e.g., AWS CloudTrail events for Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) are available and can be forwarded to your Splunk/Cloud logging.
- Redwood also emits request-level audit logs (who/when/route/model) as part of our standard enterprise telemetry. By default we retain request traces for 90 days; retention is configurable with enterprise plans.
- We offer token scrubbing and PII redaction options at ingestion time to avoid storing PII in logs. Logging of request/response payloads can be disabled per-tenant.

5) SOC 2 artifacts / compliance evidence: 
- Attaching a SOC 2 summary (SOC2-summary.pdf) and our CMEK guide (redwood_cmek_guide.pdf). For deeper evidence/attestation we have a SOC 2 point of contact in Security — I’ve included the link to the security page below.

Additional operational notes: 
- In-transit: all API traffic uses TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; mutual TLS is available for Private deployments.
- Key compromise / emergency: we support key revocation workflows. If a KEK becomes unavailable we can re-route to fallback keys under an agreed runbook; for hosted customers this requires preconfigured fallback KEKs and an escalation playbook.
- Data residency: you can pin region (us-west) — keys remain in the region’s KMS when using provider-managed KMS resources. For stricter residency we recommend a Private deployment where keys and data never leave your VPC/controlled environment.

If useful I can put together a short architecture diagram (attached) with the envelope encryption flow and an example AWS/GCP configuration snippets.
